paper.title: Instruct2Act: Mapping Multi-modality Instructions to Robotic Actions with Large Language Model
paper.central_claim: Instruct2Act is a general-purpose robotic framework that maps multimodal instructions to executable perception-and-action Python with LLMs and foundation-model APIs, attaining competitive performance on six VIMABench meta-tasks without task-specific model training.

evidence.quote: the Segment Anything Model (SAM) accurately locates candidate objects, and CLIP classifies them.
evidence.support_explanation: The perception foundation models and their separate roles are explicit; this is API orchestration, not a newly trained visuomotor policy.

evidence.quote: are stored in an environment cache
evidence.support_explanation: Images and image-to-robot transformations cross the model/controller seam through a shared cache; calibration is an assumption.

evidence.quote: We then use the Hungarian algorithm to determine the correspondences between the target scene image and the currently observed images.
evidence.support_explanation: Scene rearrangement delegates assignment to a classical solver; other tasks use SAM/CLIP and primitives.

evidence.quote: Task success rates were evaluated on 150 instances for each of the six meta-tasks, with three random seeds selected per meta-task to obtain average success rates.
evidence.support_explanation: Denominators and seed averaging are given; this is author-reported simulation evaluation.

evidence.quote: The VIMABench simulator determined task success if the final states matched the configurations outlined in the instructions.
evidence.support_explanation: Success is judged by environment state rather than an unaudited LLM completion label.

evidence.support_explanation: Published VIMA-family baselines were reused, not rerun in a fully matched harness/model/budget design.

signatures.object: LLM policy program over perception and action APIs
signatures.information: Instruction text/image crops or goal image, task image/cache and predefined image-to-robot transforms; prompt contains imports, API definitions and complete in-context examples. No raw motor learning or observed on-policy student update.
signatures.operation: Generate Python that invokes SAM/CLIP retrieval, computes object locations/scene assignment and composes available pick-and-place commands.
signatures.output: Executable program and sequence of primitive robot calls.
signatures.conditions: Stable API names, sufficiently accurate SAM masks/CLIP discrimination, calibrated image-to-robot mapping and primitive coverage.
signatures.feedback: Environment execution and final-state success used for evaluation; no demonstrated autonomous program-rewrite/acceptance loop.
signatures.selection_rule: not_applicable: static harness, not improvement search; the in-context template is author-designed.
signatures.selection_data: Six VIMABench meta-tasks for evaluation; prompt-development overlap not independently audited.
signatures.persistence: Static prompts/API library and task cache; no claimed learned growing skill repository.
signatures.later_use: Reuse the same interfaces and prompt scaffold on task instances; no retained-improvement claim.
signatures.claimed_effect: Training-free multimodal manipulation with competitive task SR.
signatures.failure_boundary: Limited pick-and-place primitives; high cost and simulation only; failed perception and grounding propagate into action.

signatures.object: Perception interface preprocessing and mask cleanup
signatures.information: Scene images and SAM candidate masks; simulator-generated task descriptions assist language instruction construction, not a proven non-privileged physical scene pipeline.
signatures.operation: Preprocess image; filter size, apply morphology and NMS to masks; use CLIP features to retrieve targets.
signatures.output: Cleaner object candidates for policy code.
signatures.conditions: Object size thresholds and preprocessing remain appropriate to the VIMABench visual regime.
signatures.selection_rule: not_applicable: fixed pipeline choices; ablation reports variants rather than online admission.
signatures.selection_data: Reported L1–L3 task evaluation; no independent prompt-search validation split established.
signatures.persistence: Fixed processing code, no episodic learning.
signatures.claimed_effect: No processing mean 51.0%, mask-only 83.0%, full 84.1% in processing study; not interchangeable with Table 1 L1 mean.
signatures.failure_boundary: Image-only processing 50.0%; improvements mostly carried by mask cleanup, not proof of general architectural novelty.

gap.author_gap: Language-only robot code interfaces and separately trained task-specific visuomotor pipelines do not directly offer one flexible multimodal instruction-to-action interface.
gap.checked_gap: A concrete interface bottleneck is demonstrated: visual candidate errors substantially lower SR and scene-goal instructions require grounding plus assignment; training-free code composition is plausible but not wholly new.

claims.text: Competitive multimodal instruction-to-action performance without task-specific training.
claims.setting: Six VIMABench meta-tasks, first three generalization levels; PyBullet.
claims.baseline_control: Published VIMA/Gato/Flamingo-style results; Table 1 VIMA-20M mean 84.4 equals Ours-Multi mean 84.4.
claims.selection_vs_test: Evaluation instances/seeds stated; no independent prompt-development-overlap audit; no success-driven persistent optimization.
claims.result_denominator: 150 instances/meta-task; three seeds/meta-task. L1 Ours-Multi [91.3,81.4,98.2,78.5,72.0,85.2], mean84.4. Not uniformly higher across tasks.
counterevidence: Published baselines not rerun with equal models/budgets.
claims.allowed_conclusion: A competitive modular simulation baseline, not an autonomous universal robot or an isolated causal win for the LLM interface.

claims.setting: Processing-module ablation across reported VIMABench settings.
claims.baseline_control: No processing, image-only, mask-only and both.
claims.selection_vs_test: Static module ablation; no separate selection/test proof for hyperparameters.
claims.result_denominator: Reported means 51.0 none,50.0 image-only,83.0 mask-only,84.1 both; general evaluation protocol supplies 150 instances and3 seeds/meta-task. No task-level variance/CI given.
counterevidence: Small extra gain from image preprocessing; no proof that hierarchical prompting or shared representation is the dominant cause.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Mask cleanup is a major measured contributor in this simulator.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported environment-scored simulation supports training-free code/API multimodal manipulation and a large mask-processing effect on six meta-tasks. Original general-purpose positioning remains broader than physical skill/latency/generalization evidence.
